After auto-compaction the agent re-attaches previously-invoked skills under TWO budgets, not one: a per-skill cap V3o=5000 TOKENS that truncates content to t*4 - marker.length chars, and a combined cap K3o=25000 tokens across all skills that DROPS a skill outright by setting its stored content to empty. The char figure is DERIVED ARITHMETIC (20000 - 98 = 19,902) with no such literal in the bundle; the marker is 98 chars, and a widely-repeated 19,900 assumes 100. The combined budget is consumed by POST-truncation sizes (d=xc(u), not xc(a.content)), so a huge skill contributes its capped 5,000 rather than its real size -- more skills fit than expected, and since the loop sorts most-recently-invoked FIRST, the skill that silently vanishes is rarely the big one but whichever was invoked least recently when the budget ran out. FOUR conditions the naive statement misses: write-back and zeroing are BOTH guarded by !c (skipped when the content is already in the conversation body), an already-attached skill is skipped entirely, and `if(!a.content) continue` is what makes zeroing PERSISTENT for the session rather than re-evaluated per compaction. The disk file is never touched, so Read recovers the full text -- which is what the truncation marker instructs. Constants are UNCHANGED across 2.1.222 -> 2.1.246 -> 2.1.247 while the minified names rotated at every build (Nvy/$vy -> V3o/K3o -> XJo/ZJo): pin values, not names. DELIBERATELY NOT CLAIMED: the token estimator xc/Lc is a cross-chunk import and is NOT resolved (three same-named functions in the region, none a counter), so Math.round(chars/4) is consistent with the t*4 but is not asserted here and 'binary-verified' applied to it is an over-claim. The finding came from two documents agreeing with each other and disagreeing with the artifact: agreement between derived sources is not corroboration, it is frequently the moment before the first check. v2.41.3 corrects two errors of this skill's own.
